lede: Five numbers describe a whole set of data: the smallest, the largest, the middle, and the two quarter marks either side of it. Draw them on a scale and you have a box plot, the picture used to put two sets of waiting times side by side and see at a glance which is which.
can: Read all five values off a box plot, and the range and interquartile range with them.
Turn a range or an interquartile range given in words into the missing value.
Compare two distributions with one sentence on average and one on spread.

text: Box plots: five numbers, one picture

md: A box plot is the five-figure summary drawn on a scale: **minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile, maximum**. The box holds the middle half of the data, the line inside it is the median, and the two whiskers reach the extremes. It is the fastest way to compare two sets of data, which is why CCEA almost always follows a box plot with the instruction to make two comparisons.

prompt: Which part of a box plot shows the median?
options: The left-hand edge of the box
The middle of the whole scale
explain: The line inside the box. It is often off-centre, and that itself tells you the data is not symmetrical.

title: Not on the formula sheet
md:
$\text{maximum} = \text{minimum} + \text{range}$ and $\text{minimum} = \text{maximum} - \text{range}$

$\text{UQ} = \text{LQ} + \text{IQR}$ and $\text{LQ} = \text{UQ} - \text{IQR}$

Each of the four sections of the plot holds a quarter of the data. None of this is printed anywhere in the exam.

prompt: From the picture above, what is the interquartile range of the waiting times, in minutes?
explain: The width of the box: $45 - 26 = 19$ minutes. The range, whisker to whisker, is 56.

title: Why the long whisker holds no more data
md: Each of the four sections is a quarter of the values, so a wide section means the values there are spread out, not that there are more of them. The long right-hand whisker above covers the slowest quarter of the patients, thinly scattered between 45 and 68 minutes.

prompt: A box plot's right-hand whisker is three times as long as its box. What does that tell you?
options: The slowest quarter is spread out
There are more values in the whisker
answer: The slowest quarter is spread out
explain: Every section holds a quarter of the data, so a longer section means those values are more spread out, not that there are more of them.

md:
A CCEA question rarely hands you five positions. It hands you a mixture, like this:

maximum 96%, median 40%, lower quartile 28%, range 84%, interquartile range 24%.

Three of those are **positions** on the scale. Two are **widths**: a range of 84 does not mean anyone scored 84%.

So before drawing: minimum $= 96 - 84 = 12$, and upper quartile $= 28 + 24 = 52$. Each of those carries its own mark.

prompt: A data set has maximum 96 and range 84. What is the minimum?
explain: $96 - 84 = 12$. The range is the whole distance from the smallest value to the largest.

prompt: The lower quartile is 28 and the interquartile range is 24. What is the upper quartile?
explain: $28 + 24 = 52$. The interquartile range is the width of the box, so it is added on to the left-hand edge.

title: Drawing and Reading Box Plots
why: The drawing routine end to end. Watch the order: the box between the quartiles first, then the median line, then the whiskers.

prompt: In the video, what is drawn first?
answer: The box between the two quartiles
explain: Yes. The box fixes the scale of the drawing, and the median line and whiskers are added to it.
options: The box between the two quartiles
The median line on its own

md:
Two box plots on the same scale is an invitation to make **two comparisons**, and the two marks are deliberately different: one for an **average**, one for **spread**.

- Average: compare the **medians**, then say what it means. *Moira's median is greater, so callers there waited longer on average.*
- Spread: compare the **interquartile ranges**, then say what it means. *Larne's interquartile range is smaller, so its waits were more consistent.*

Two sentences about medians earn one mark, not two. A sentence that only quotes numbers earns none.

prompt: Fill the gap: two box plots are compared with one sentence about an average and one about ______.
explain: Spread. The words spread, variation or consistent are what the second comparison mark is looking for.

prompt: Which pair of statements would earn both comparison marks?
options: Moira's median is greater, so callers wait longer there; Larne's interquartile range is smaller, so Larne is more consistent
Moira's median is 11 and Larne's is 6; Moira's interquartile range is 11 and Larne's is 4
Moira's median is greater, so callers wait longer; Moira's maximum is also greater
answer: Moira's median is greater, so callers wait longer there; Larne's interquartile range is smaller, so Larne is more consistent
explain: One average sentence and one spread sentence, both saying what the difference means. Quoting the four values earns nothing, and two average sentences earn one mark.

title: Comparisons must interpret
md: Summer 2024 M3 Q26(b) asked for two comparisons and reports that valid statistical comparisons, as opposed to quoted values, were not made. The M4 report on the same series adds that most candidates said one median was higher but few used the word spread or variation for the interquartile range.

prompt: Both of a candidate's comparisons are about the medians. How many of the two marks are earned?
explain: One mark is for an average and the other for spread, so a second median sentence adds nothing. Compare the interquartile ranges for the second mark.

text: Why the interquartile range, and what a sample can tell you

md:
When a question asks **why** the interquartile range represents a data set better than the range, it is asking about **that** data set. The competition scores above are a good example: one entry of 96% sits far above the rest and drags the range up to 84. The interquartile range of 24 ignores it.

The sentence that earns the mark names the value. "The interquartile range is not affected by extremes" is true, and it earns nothing.

A box plot of a **sample** describes the sample. Another sample would give different quartiles, so a comparison of two samples is evidence about those samples, not proof about the whole population.

prompt: Which reason would earn the mark for a data set whose maximum is 96% when everything else is below 60%?
options: The 96% is far above the rest, so it stretches the range but leaves the interquartile range alone
The interquartile range is not affected by extreme values
The interquartile range is a more accurate measure
answer: The 96% is far above the rest, so it stretches the range but leaves the interquartile range alone
explain: It names the value in this data set. The other two are general statements, and neither scored in November 2025.

md:
Read all five values, the range and the interquartile range off a box plot.
Turn a range or an interquartile range into the value it hides.
Compare two plots with one sentence on average and one on spread.

The usual shape is a four-mark plot drawn from five statistics, two of which you work out first, then a one-mark explain-why; sometimes it is two printed plots and make two comparisons. The first marks are the calculated values, so list all five before drawing. The last is the plot itself, ruled and complete. Stuck: name the value unlike the rest and say what it does to the range.
